answer: Plant one shared orchard, not a thousand private plots: the economy keeps a single evolving artifact, and each epoch only one graft is accepted — the proposal that best extends the last stranger's work, measured with quartz-precise checks against the living state. A sybil farm can forge a thousand copies, but they all queue for the same single slot and must each re-read the newest growth; mass production buys no parallel advantage, and clones competing with themselves dilute their own odds.
